subject: maths
title: Transformations — rotation, reflection, translation, enlargement

slides.heading: Transformations — four ways to move or resize a shape
slides.body: A transformation moves or changes a shape in a precise, rule-based way. There are four types: translation (sliding without turning), reflection (flipping in a mirror line), rotation (turning around a fixed point), and enlargement (scaling up or down from a centre point). The original shape is called the object and the result is called the image. Describing a transformation fully means stating the type and every piece of information needed to reproduce it exactly — marks are lost for partial descriptions.
slides.note: Maximum 3 sentences. Plain English. No AQA references. What is this and why does it matter.

slides.heading: What to state for each transformation
slides.formula: Translation: vector (x over y) where x is right (+) or left (−) and y is up (+) or down (−)  |  Reflection: the equation of the mirror line  |  Rotation: angle, direction (clockwise/anticlockwise), centre of rotation  |  Enlargement: scale factor, centre of enlargement
slides.formulaExplained: Translation uses a column vector — top number is the horizontal shift (positive = right), bottom number is the vertical shift (positive = up). Reflection needs the mirror line written as an equation (e.g. y = x, x = 3). Rotation needs an angle (e.g. 90°), a direction, and the coordinates of the fixed point it rotates around. Enlargement needs the scale factor (if it's between 0 and 1, the image is smaller) and the centre point. For enlargement, image distance from centre = scale factor × object distance from centre.
slides.whenToUse: Any question asking you to perform or describe a transformation. Always name the type first, then provide all required information in a logical order.
slides.note: Show formula in standard notation. Explain each variable. State when this formula applies.

slides.heading: Let's work through one
slides.question: Triangle A has vertices at (1, 1), (3, 1) and (3, 4). Translate it by the vector (−4 over 2). Write the coordinates of the image.

steps.instruction: Add the column vector to each vertex. The top number (−4) is added to each x-coordinate; the bottom number (+2) is added to each y-coordinate.
Apply the same vector to the second vertex.
Apply the same vector to the third vertex.

slides.conclusion: The image triangle has vertices at (−3, 3), (−1, 3) and (−1, 6).
slides.note: Numbers must differ from any question in the question bank for this subtopic.

slides.heading: Watch out for this

mistakes.mistake: Describing a rotation without stating the centre — writing '90° clockwise' with no coordinates.
mistakes.correction: A rotation is not fully described without all three elements: angle, direction, and centre. Write e.g. 'Rotation, 90° clockwise, about the point (0, 0)'.

mistakes.mistake: Confusing the direction of a translation vector — adding the y-value to x or treating a negative as going up.
mistakes.correction: In a column vector, the top number always acts on x (left–right) and the bottom always acts on y (up–down). Negative top = move left; negative bottom = move down.

mistakes.mistake: Using a scale factor for enlargement without locating the centre — drawing the enlarged shape in the wrong position on the grid.
mistakes.correction: For each vertex of the object, draw a ray from the centre of enlargement through the vertex and extend it. The image vertex sits on that ray at a distance equal to scale factor × original distance from the centre.

slides.note: Minimum 2, maximum 3 mistakes. Specific not generic.

keyFacts.fact: To fully describe a rotation: state angle, direction (clockwise or anticlockwise), and the coordinates of the centre of rotation.
keyFacts.examTip: Losing one of these three elements loses a mark. Write all three even if the question seems to imply one of them.

keyFacts.fact: A translation is described by a column vector, not words like 'move 3 right and 2 down'. The top is horizontal movement (+ = right), the bottom is vertical (+ = up).
keyFacts.examTip: Write the column vector with a proper bracket, not as a fraction — examiners distinguish the two.

keyFacts.fact: For an enlargement, scale factor = image length ÷ object length. If the scale factor is between 0 and 1, the image is smaller than the object.
keyFacts.examTip: A negative scale factor places the image on the opposite side of the centre — the shape is both scaled and flipped through the centre.

note: keyFacts: 2-4 entries. Exam-precise language. These are what Mabel writes into her notes.
